claim: "one reviewer questions whether papers were mailed" (opportunity 3)
problem: The paraphrase inverts the direction of the disagreement in the cited review. Read in full on the Google listing, that reviewer says the attorney told him he had NOT mailed a package of legal papers, while the reviewer states he did receive papers from the office ('Semantics? Perhaps.'). As written, the audit implies a client was unsure whether papers had been sent, which the review contradicts.
fix: Reword to match the source, e.g. 'one reviewer's account differs from the attorney's over whether papers were mailed', or replace with the safer already-supported point that document logistics come up in the reviews.

claim: Both negative Google reviews are used as present-tense evidence under "What's happening now" (opportunities 2 and 3)
problem: Google dates all four reviews '8 years ago' (i.e. roughly 2018). The audit never says the reviews are old, so a reader reasonably reads them as describing current service — unfair to the firm and materially weaker as evidence of today's calendar handling.
fix: Add a date qualifier, e.g. 'one reviewer (c. 2018) describes two cancelled appointments', and keep the 'worth checking together' framing as the live question.

problem: The site has six .php pages — index, about-us, practice-areas, overview, contact-us and directions. Five is the number of nav items; directions.php is a live sixth page that also carries the header image and the Manalapan footer.
fix: Say 'rebuild the five menu pages plus the directions page' or simply 'rebuild all six pages'.

claim: Automation shares and handling times behind all three impact ranges (25/40/15 minutes and 70–85% / 40–60% / 50–70% automated)
problem: Only the volumes are flagged as 'our assumption'. The per-enquiry minutes and the automation percentages drive the hours and are presented without either a label or a source; the 70–85% figure in opportunity 1 is also well above the automation shares used in the underlying analysis (40–60% for intake) and is not supported by any benchmark cited in the dossier. The dollars themselves are small and not alarmist, but the framing invites the reader to treat the percentages as measured.
fix: Mark handling times and automation shares as assumptions ('our assumption' on each), and either lower the opportunity-1 band toward the analysis.json figure or add one line stating that no firm-level benchmark exists so the shares are illustrative.

problem: The 1.25 benefits loading is unsourced and unlabelled; the two medians behind it are correct, but a reader cannot see where 1.25 comes from. (It appears conservative rather than inflated, which is why this is a labelling issue, not an accuracy one.)
fix: Add '(our assumption; conservative benefits loading)' after ×1.25.

claim: Walk-in opener: "I am local to Milltown Road"
problem: This is an unverified claim about the sender, not the business, and it is geographically ambiguous: 77 Milltown Road is in East Brunswick, while the consultancy is in Milltown borough and the firm's own site says Manalapan. Said to a lawyer, an imprecise local claim invites exactly the scrutiny the audit is trying to earn trust for.
fix: Use something checkable and true of the sender ('I'm based in Milltown, a few minutes from your office'), or drop the local line and open on the before-and-after.
